known_conditions: GET /readyz returns 503 on business_query_resolver_coverage: app/policy/manifest/index.json accepts a legacy manifest hash (7a413053) that no bundle declares compatibility with. Confirmed pre-existing - the index has no diff against master, and no bundle on master covered it either. Does NOT gate the Ask panel, which probes /healthz. Not a suite failure.

The deployment is intentionally SQL-only while its document provider is unavailable. The eight legacy document cases (rb-07..rb-12, rt-01b) are visibly NOT RUN and their corpus/index/embedding preflights are conditional. Do not re-enable Azure, ingest documents, or let a document prerequisite block structured cases in this run.

settings.record_analytics_mode is `disabled` in this environment. Follow-up chips therefore never offer count / group-by prompts, only 'Show the most recent <resource>'. fu-01's expected chip set assumes this; if analytics is enabled, update it.

Two databases are live on this host and they are not the same one. The billing app (artisan serve, login, record views) reads mcp_local; the RAG container reads mcp_prod_wire_eval (MCP_BILLING_DATABASE_URL and MCP_RECORD_DATABASE_URL). Derive every oracle from mcp_prod_wire_eval - that is the database the answer comes from, and it is what environment.database names. Verified 2026-08-31: the projection fact tables hold identical row counts in both, and the only users-row difference is test_admin, which exists in mcp_local only. That does not affect answers: no module under app/ reads a users table, and caller identity plus permissions arrive in the signed JWT record_access claim (app/auth/jwt.py:89-99, 155-170; ScopeValues in app/auth/record_access.py:48-56 accepts department_id only, extra=forbid). Admin-persona cases are therefore runnable.
